questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code manages file and socket descriptors? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
upload_manifest is called with a path that does not exist. What happens?
choices: It resolves the host and connects first, then reports the open failure from the done label
It returns UPLOAD_ERR_IO, because fopen failures are reported as read errors
It returns UPLOAD_ERR_OPEN immediately, without calling dial()
It jumps to done and calls fclose(NULL), which is harmless

questions.prompt: fread() returns a short count partway through the file because of a disk read error. What does upload_manifest do?
choices: It reports UPLOAD_ERR_IO via ferror(fp), after which done closes the socket and the file
It sends the remaining bytes as zeros so the receiver sees the declared length
It treats the short read as end of file, half-closes the socket and returns UPLOAD_OK
It returns immediately with UPLOAD_ERR_IO and leaves the socket to be closed on process exit

questions.prompt: The receiver stops reading, its TCP window fills, and the SO_SNDTIMEO of 10 seconds expires during send(). What does the caller of upload_manifest observe?
choices: send blocks forever, because SO_SNDTIMEO applies only to connect
send_all retries forever, because EAGAIN is treated like EINTR
The process receives SIGPIPE and terminates
send fails, send_all returns -1, and upload_manifest returns UPLOAD_ERR_SEND, possibly after part of the file was delivered
